content:
anna_devex: Heads-up — baking the AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 results into a stable packaging + deploy guidance doc. Need final consensus on naming, minimal accuracy thresholds, and what we mark as "safe-for-dedicated" vs "experimental".

josh_engml: +1. can we lock on one canonical filename scheme so infra + optimizer can parse it?

kai_research: Suggestion: modelname__quant__impl__deltaX__latencyTier\.
Example: `llama3-13b__awq__awq-4bit__d0.7__p50` where d0.7 = median accuracy delta vs fp16 (in %), p50 = 50th percentile latency tier.

priya_prod: That looks parseable. We should also include a runtime compatibility tag (cuda-cu121, triton-2, onnx-runtime) — otherwise ops will get mismatched profiles.

cheng_infra: +1 for runtime tag. How about ordering: `model__impl__runtime__delta` so the manifest filename maps to storage layout? e.g. `llama3-13b__gptq__cuda-cu121__d0.9__.qprof`

anna_devex: Good. What about semantics for the delta sign? absolute vs relative? We should standardize: delta = (quant_metric - fp16_metric) * 100, positive means worse. Use median over our eval set.

kai_research: Agreed. Also recommend we publish three numeric thresholds in the profile metadata (all relative to fp16):
- accuracy_median_delta_pct
- accuracy_95pct_delta_pct
- embedding_cosine_drop_pct (for embedding models)

josh_engml: For deployment gating propose:
- safe-for-hosted: median_delta <= 1.2% AND 95pct_delta <= 4% AND no >8% outliers
- safe-for-dedicated: median_delta <= 2% AND 95pct_delta <= 6%
- experimental: anything worse, flagged in profile and requires manual approval

priya_prod: Those thresholds seem fine but we should tweak per workload type. For rerank/classification tasks even 1% can matter; for summarization we can allow slightly higher. We need `workload_hint` in the profile: [classification, summarization, instruction-following, embeddings, code].

anna_devex: Nice call. We'll add `workload_hint`. Also need a short deployment note string that infra can surface e.g. "recommended_max_concurrent_requests", "expected_memory_delta".

cheng_infra: On packaging: produce a single compressed artifact with: `qprofile.json` (flat fields), `metrics.csv` (selected eval rows), `runtime_hints.txt` and `checksums.txt`. Name the tarball using the canonical filename scheme and semver: `llama3-13b__awq__cuda-cu121__d0.7__p50__v0.1.qpkg.tar.gz`

kai_research: Example qprofile.json schema (flattened):
```
model: "llama3-13b"
quant_impl: "awq-4bit"
runtime: "cuda-cu121"
version: "0.1"
workload_hint: "instruction-following"
accuracy_median_delta_pct: "0.7"
accuracy_95pct_delta_pct: "3.4"
embedding_cosine_drop_pct: "0.12"
recommended_max_concurrent_requests: "40"
expected_gpu_mem_increase_mb: "-200"
notes: "uses prefix-KV caching; fallback to fp16 on OOM"
```

priya_prod: We should add `acceptance_signoff` field (list of teams/names) and `release_channel` (hosted/dedicated/private/experimental). Ops can auto-block installs missing signoff for restricted channels.

anna_devex: Agree. One more ops ask: include a short deterministic test snippet in the package so infra can run a quick smoke check. e.g. `--smoke-prompt "Summarize: The quick brown fox"` and expected tokens prefix.

josh_engml: Bakeoff result summary idea: include a one-line human summary in metrics.csv header like: "median delta 0.7%, latency +12% @ batch1, cost -32%". Helps PMs review quickly.

kai_research: Also add an `eval-id` linking back to the experiment run in our internal eval DB (so we can reproduce exact dataset split & seed).

anna_devex: I'll draft the packaging spec and upload to the docs repo. Action items:
- kai: finalize qprofile.json flattened keys + examples (due EOD Wed)
- josh: codify gating thresholds into optimize rules (feature flags)
- cheng: implement runtime tag parsing and install blocker for missing signoffs
- priya: define per-workload tweak recommendations

optimize-bot: Reminder: new qprofile uploaded to staging will trigger `qprofile-eval` job. Use `optimize-cli qprofile upload --staging`.

anna_devex: Cool — once we have Kai's example I'll push a small RFC. Thanks all :rocket:
